title: Alone Together with Perplexing Ruins and the Dungeon Dive - Episode 2
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dnUUMRDbasE

Daniel (@dungeondive) and Allan of Perplexing Ruins return for a second conversation, now with a name for the show. It opens on the economics of the small-press scene — art packs, game jams, patreon tiers — and Allan's argument that leaving reviews on itch.io is a low-cost way to support people whose living depends on visibility. Both are candid about relying on systems outside their control: Allan on commissions, Daniel on the YouTube algorithm and a channel income he describes as below minimum wage.

The episode's real substance arrives when the conversation turns to combat and character death. Daniel makes the case that heroes in sword and sorcery fiction don't die because there'd be no story left to read — so treat each session as a short story in a character's life, and interpret a fatal roll as loss, injury, or abduction rather than an ending. Allan agrees and pushes further: reduce enemies to threat tiers (a rat is a one, a dragon a four), skip attrition, and let the sixth encounter be the narrative hook rather than the sixth slog.

They also discuss *Rune*, *Sacrifice*, and — a genuine curveball — *Deadball*, a dice-driven baseball management game.

----

How do you handle character death in solo play — reroll, or narrate your way out of it?
